narrative: The model estimated an 86% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied. This means that, based on the information supplied, the model saw a high likelihood of repayment difficulty. The most important factor was your checking-account status: being overdrawn (<0 DM) pushed the decision toward bad credit, and this is uncommon among approved applicants, only about 13% of whom were in that category. The second most important factor was your credit history, recorded as “all paid at bank.” Although that may sound positive, it is rare among approved applicants—only about 3%—and it pushed the prediction toward bad credit. The third factor was property status: having no known property pushed toward bad credit, compared with approved applicants where property such as a car, real estate, or savings/life insurance is common. To improve a future application, bring your checking account into positive balance, obtain documented proof that your credit history is correctly recorded and up to date, and build or document savings and assets; adding a guarantor or applying for a smaller amount with a lower installment burden could also help. You may also ask the lender how to correct or supplement the information used.
